subject: Realtime token-drip causing throughput & latency spike (urgent)
messages:
From: Sophie Chan <sophie.chan@rivermark.com>
To: markus.klein@redwood.ai, vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai
Cc: support@rivermark.com
Date: Thu, 3 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Realtime stream producing tiny token "drip" — severe latency/throughput impact

Hi Markus / Vanessa,

We're seeing a serious issue with the realtime endpoint in our production ingest. Over the last 45 minutes requests that previously produced ~120 tokens/sec are returning as a steady stream of single-token chunks spaced 800-1500ms apart. The client is effectively starved — throughput has dropped ~60% and tail latency is spiking.

I attached a short log and a HAR from a failing demo: rivermark-stream-log.txt (contains headers and chunk timing). The behavior started after a deployment window on our side but we've rolled back and the problem persists.

Examples: token chunks arrive slowly and sockets stay open but idle between chunks. We see occasional 200 OK with chunked transfer but long inter-chunk gaps. No obvious 5xx from your side.

Impact: several users hit timeouts and the UI shows partial responses; this is affecting a paid flow (weekly quota heavy). We need an estimate for mitigation and whether this is an SLA-impacting incident.

Can your SRE team triage? Happy to jump on a call.

Thanks,
Sophie Chan
Senior PM, Integrations
Rivermark Health

Triage notes (initial):
- Ingress logs show normal 200s on the model tier, but our edge proxy (edge-02/us-west) is emitting chunk boundary events where chunk payload size is 1-3 bytes repeatedly. CPU/memory on model nodes look fine.
- There are intermittent spikes in our internal keepalive retransmits to the proxy around 08:50-09:05 PDT. That correlates with client's first failure window.
- I ran a quick trace and saw that our chunk coalescer is not merging small frames due to a heuristics regression introduced in the batching optimizer (CL 18294). The optimizer set the coalescing threshold to 1 for low-latency paths which allows many tiny frames out.

Proposed immediate mitigation: revert CL 18294 on the gateway for the affected hostpool, enable conservative coalescing (threshold >= 16 bytes) and restart the proxy group. That should restore normal token burst behavior.

I've attached a short trace extract: sre-trace-20260903.json.

I'll coordinate the change with infra ops; ETA for the revert + rolling restart is ~25 minutes once we have approvals.

-David

Team,

Urgent — Rivermark is a strategic Mid-Market account (annual commit + integrations). If their paid flow continues to see degraded throughput we risk a renewal/regression conversation. Vanessa, David — thanks for triage. We need to:

1) Move to the proposed mitigation immediately (revert batching optimizer CL and restart edge proxies for their hostpool).
2) Open an incident bridge and invite engineering/product leadership for 30-minute sync (I'm pulling in Kimberly).
3) Notify sales/account execs and prepare a short customer-facing note with timeline and an apology credit offer if we miss SLA.

Please confirm when the revert is queued and whether we need an exec sign-off for the proxy restart. If the change risks affecting other hostpools, we should canary to 10% first — but Rivermark is on a tight window and would prefer a faster fix.

Markus Klein
VP, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

Thanks Markus. Please proceed with the revert and rolling restart but canary to the Rivermark hostpool first (10% -> 50% -> 100%) and monitor token inter-arrival times and 5xx rates.

I will schedule a 15-minute exec sync in 45 minutes to review impact and next steps. If the canary is negative, be prepared to trigger the controlled fallback to a compatible model variant with aggressive coalescing (we've used that successfully in previous incidents).

Also, prepare a short postmortem timeline and a recommended customer credit that maps to the perceived SLA breach window.

-Kimberly
Head of Sales Ops
